assumptions.label: Years counted
assumptions.why: Transit buildings usually serve 40 years or more. The Region has not published the hub's design life.

assumptions.label: Discount rate
assumptions.why: At 0% every year's dollar counts the same. A higher rate counts future dollars for less, as many public-sector cost studies do (3% is common).

assumptions.label: Yearly upkeep (maintenance and repair)
assumptions.why: No upkeep figure is published. A common rule of thumb for public buildings is 2 to 4% of their value a year for maintenance and repair (US National Research Council, 1990). We start at 2% of the capital budget.

assumptions.label: Yearly running cost (staff, cleaning, security, utilities)
assumptions.why: No running cost is published, and the operations agreements are still to come. It starts at $0 so the chart shows only what is known; move it to test an amount.

assumptions.label: Capital cost overrun
assumptions.why: Large building projects often cost more than first budgeted. Slide to see what an overrun adds.

assumptions.label: Households sharing the cost
assumptions.why: 222,426 households lived in Waterloo Region at the 2021 Census (Statistics Canada). There are more now. Businesses pay too, so this is a rough share per home, not a bill.

method: Lifecycle cost = capital in the years it is spent + operating and maintenance in each year of service + renewals in the years they fall + emissions × carbon price (none counted here), over the years shown, in today's dollars, undiscounted unless a discount rate is set. Built in code by lenses/cost from figures whose quotes were checked on their pages; everything else is a labelled assumption.
inputNotes: Capital: projects 90170 (early works) and 90179 (the hub) by year from the 2026 budget book (cited), $163.5 million in all. This matches the report's $35 million and $129 million.
Service starts in 2031, between substantial completion (2030) and the end-2031 target (both cited).
Upkeep: 2% of capital a year (assumption, slider 0–4%). Running cost: $0 by default (unknown, slider).
No separate renewal is counted. The upkeep rule of thumb is meant to cover repairs and replacing parts.
Emissions are not counted: no document gives the hub's emissions.
The minor variances being decided don't change these costs; the costs show what the hub they enable commits the Region to.
unknowns: What the hub will cost to run and maintain each year, and how that is shared with Metrolinx and GO Transit.
What the Region will earn or spend on the leftover land after the hub is built.
summary:
LIFECYCLE COST over 40 years (2026-2065), service from 2031, discount rate 0.0%, today's dollars:
- Capital $163.5 million (59%)
- Operating $0 (0%)
- Maintenance $114.4 million (41%)
- Renewal $0 (0%)
- Environmental (emissions x carbon price) $0 (0%)
- Lifecycle total $277.9 million; the upfront price is 59% of it.
- Per household (222,426 households): $1,250 over the period, about $31 a year.
